diagnostic_evidence.quote: Apply matrix Chernoff inequality (\cref{thm:chernoff}) conditionally, and then removing the conditioning

issues.failure_explanation: Matrix Chernoff is invoked for the law of the summands conditioned on the event that every summand has norm at most Delta, which is what supplies the uniform bound L = Delta. Under that conditional law the mean is E[S_k | ||S_k|| <= Delta], not W^T E[w w^T] W = I. Truncating PSD summands removes mass E[S_k 1{||S_k||>Delta}], so the conditional lambda_min can be below ell. Thus mu_min = ell, and similarly mu_max = ell||Z||_2^2, are not verified for the conditional distribution. The tail bounds in Steps 1 and 2 are therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Chernoff to truncated summands S_k 1{||S_k||<=Delta}, which coincide with S_k on the event E. Bound ||E[S_k 1{||S_k||>Delta}]|| via Cauchy-Schwarz, using the moment bounds from lem:kronrank1 and the tail probability delta/(4 ell). Then use the adjusted mu_min = ell(1-eta) and mu_max, and adjust the sample-size constants.
issues.overall_effect: The probabilistic guarantees of the key lemma are unproven, and with them the range-finder, single-view, RHOSVD-KRP, RSTHOSVD-KRP and subspace-embedding results, all of which reuse this conditioning argument.
issues.title: Matrix Chernoff applied conditionally on a truncation event but with the unconditional mean
issues.why_classification: The fix needs a contained new truncation lemma and some constant changes. The proof architecture and the rates survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Setting (N-r)exp(-eps^2 mu_max/((2+eps)Delta)) = delta/4 gives eps^2/(2+eps) = Gamma. The positive root is eps* = (Gamma + sqrt(Gamma^2+8Gamma))/2. One has eps* <= 2Gamma only if Gamma >= 1. For Gamma < 1, which is the typical regime since Gamma is O(ln N/ell), eps* is approximately sqrt(2Gamma) and exceeds 2Gamma. Taking eps = 2Gamma therefore does not make the failure probability at most delta/4, and the bound (1+2Gamma)ell||Z||_2^2 is not established.

failure_location.quote: and choose the positive root to get $\varepsilon = 2 \Gamma$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use eps* <= Gamma + sqrt(2Gamma) <= 1/2 + 2Gamma, which follows from AM-GM. Restate the lemma and the downstream bounds with 1+Gamma+sqrt(2Gamma), or with 3/2+2Gamma, in place of 1+2Gamma.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit factor 2(1+2Gamma) in the lemma, and the factors 1+2r(1+2Gamma_i) in all downstream error bounds, are unsupported in the main regime.
issues.title: Incorrect root of the quadratic: epsilon = 2*Gamma fails when Gamma < 1
issues.why_classification: The repair is local, but every explicit stated bound must be weakened by a constant-level change. This is a limited weakening, and the O(r) form of the bound survives.

issues.failure_explanation: With delta replaced by delta/2, thm:rrf and thm:tantheta require ell_r >= 8(r + rC ln^d(16ell_r/delta))ln(8r/delta), and the analogous condition for ell_l. The stated conditions omit the factor 8, so the invoked results are used outside their hypotheses. In addition, the event E uses (1+Gamma_r) whereas thm:rrf only gives (1+2Gamma_r). The final statement has (1+Gamma_l) while the proof yields (1+2Gamma_l), and the right-hand side is written with the undefined ||Sigma_F||_2^2 instead of ||Sigma_perp||_F^2. The stated bound is therefore not what the argument supports.

failure_location.quote: The assumptions on $\ell_r$ ensure that, by \cref{thm:rrf}, $\prob\{\mc{E}^c\}\le \delta/2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require ell_r and ell_l to satisfy the thm:rrf and thm:tantheta conditions with the factor 8 at level delta/2. Restate the bound as (1+2r(1+2Gamma_r))(1+2ell_r(1+2Gamma_l))||Sigma_perp||_F^2, which is still subject to ISSUE-001 and ISSUE-002.
issues.overall_effect: The single-view guarantee for block-structured matrices is unproven as stated: both its sample sizes and its error constant are unsupported.
issues.title: Single-view theorem's sample-size hypotheses and constants do not match the invoked results
issues.why_classification: The theorem must be weakened to require larger sketch sizes and a larger constant. The result remains comparable, and no new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: E_t bounds a partial sum of mode errors. E_t does not imply E_{t+1}, because the (t+1)-th error can exceed its bound; if the inclusions held, P(E_d) >= P(E_1) would be trivial. The correct relation is E_t ∩ {mode-(t+1) bound} ⊆ E_{t+1}. In addition, the conditional step silently replaces (1+2Gamma_{t+1}) by the smaller (1+Gamma_{t+1}), which is not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the nesting claim by E_t ∩ F_{t+1} ⊆ E_{t+1}, where F_{t+1} is the mode-(t+1) range-finder event. Note that P(F_{t+1}|E_t) >= 1-delta/d by the independence of the fresh sketches, and keep the factor (1+2Gamma_{t+1}).
issues.overall_effect: The probability chaining argument for the RSTHOSVD-KRP bound rests on a false claim and contains an unjustified constant reduction.
issues.title: False nesting of events in the RSTHOSVD-KRP proof
issues.why_classification: A short local correction restores the argument, and the statement is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is slightly more favorable than our result which predicts $\ell = \mc{O}(r\ln^2(N/\delta))$ for $d=2$

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the paper's bound is O(r ln^d(N/delta)). The bound actually established, cor:subspaceembed, is O(r ln^d(N/delta) ln(r/delta)). The comparison with other subspace-embedding results therefore drops a ln(r/delta) factor from the paper's own requirement.

failure_location.quote: which predicts the number of samples to be $\mc{O}( r \ln^d (N/\delta))$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the complexity as O(r ln^d(N/delta) ln(r/delta)), and O(r ln^2(N/delta) ln(r/delta)) for d=2, and adjust the comparative remarks accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The comparisons in the discussion against Gaussian, SRHT, d=2 KRP and JL-based results understate the paper's sample requirement.
issues.title: Paper's own subspace-embedding sample complexity misstated in literature comparison
issues.why_classification: Correcting the stated complexity is a local edit, and no formal result changes.
